notes: A single brigade's AO is about a third smaller, and AOs top out smaller
Neighbouring AOs now share a boundary instead of overlapping: when a new AO opens next to one, both redraw their edges along the line between them, with only a thin overlap

Units stay inside their AOs. Outside it they have no FOB support or quick reaction force, MEDEVAC is slower, they fight at 70% and are about twice as likely to be ambushed. Units that drift out on their own pull back inside, and fallbacks and quick-reaction forces stay within the AO. Ordered assaults and raids can still cross the line
